themes_detail.label: Street Signs Deteriorating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope is experiencing a sharp spike in damaged and dangling street signs THIS WEEK, with 5 dangling sign complaints (vs. 0.4 weekly average) and 7 damaged sign complaints last week (vs. 0.9 weekly average)—a combined 1,233% and 700% increase—raising public safety and navigation concerns across the neighborhood.
evidence: Street Sign - Dangling: 5 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (1,233% increase, z-score 6.65)
Street Sign - Damaged: 7 complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (700% increase, z-score 6.61)
Both spikes represent statistically significant deviations (z-scores above 6.6) indicating non-random event
reporting_angles: Canvas specific blocks in Park Slope and Carroll Gardens to document which signs are dangling or damaged and pose hazards to pedestrians/cyclists
Interview DOT about maintenance backlog; determine if weather, vehicle strikes, or deferred maintenance is driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK Park Slope residents filed 8 complaints about abandoned bikes (vs. 1.1 weekly average)—a 611% spike with z-score 6.53—suggesting a rapid accumulation of derelict bicycles in public spaces that may signal a bike-share abandonment issue or lack of enforcement.
evidence: Abandoned Bike complaints: 8 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (611% increase, z-score 6.53)
Bike Rack complaints also spiked: 6 last week vs. 0.6 average (860% increase, z-score 4.84)
Combined signals suggest broader bike infrastructure or abandonment enforcement issue
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify hotspots; interview Parks/Sanitation about enforcement and removal timelines
Contact Citi Bike and other operators to determine if decommissioning or service cuts are driving abandonments

themes_detail.label: Building/Use Code Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints in Park Slope jumped 620% THIS WEEK and last week, from 1.2 weekly average to 9 complaints (z-score 8.0, highest severity rating), indicating a possible wave of unpermitted occupancy, zoning violations, or illegal conversions coinciding with active ULURP rezonings in the district.
evidence: Building/Use violations: 9 complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (620% increase, z-score 8.0, highest z-score in dataset)
1,122 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (699 alterations, 146 new buildings, 29 demolitions) indicate active construction/alteration climate
Three active land-use applications (46 Nelson Street Rezoning, GSD certifications) suggest neighborhood-wide development pressure
reporting_angles: FOIL DOB violation notices from past 2 weeks; identify patterns (illegal conversions, unpermitted work, zoning violations) and geographic clusters
Interview DOE/DOB about whether rezoning uncertainty is spurring pre-emptive or non-compliant development; cross-reference with community board concerns about affordable housing and zoning

themes_detail.label: Tree Infrastructure Failing
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope is reporting multiple tree-related complaints—7 overgrown tree/branches complaints THIS WEEK (409% above baseline) and a spike in dead/dying trees 3 weeks ago (1,100% spike)—suggesting deferred maintenance of Parks Department tree inventory and potential safety hazards from branches and dead wood.
evidence: Overgrown Tree/Branches: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average (409% increase, z-score 5.67)
Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Community Board budget request (annual recurring) for 'Reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park' and park safety enhancements suggests long-term neglect
reporting_angles: Walk major streets (Prospect Park West, Seventh Avenue) and parks to photo-document overgrown branches and dead trees; compile list of specific locations
Interview Parks Department about tree maintenance budget and trim/removal backlog; investigate if winter weather or staffing shortages are factors

themes_detail.label: Consumer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: THIS WEEK and last week Park Slope saw consumer complaints rise 188% to 9 complaints vs. 3.1 weekly average (z-score 4.63), suggesting a possible local retail or service quality issue worth investigating for patterns.
evidence: Consumer Complaint: 9 complaints last week vs. 3.1 weekly average (188% increase, z-score 4.63)
Complaint category is broad; specific businesses/services not identified in dataset
reporting_angles: FOIL detailed 311 consumer complaint records to identify target businesses, complaint types, and resolution status
Reach out to local small business association or block associations to cross-check emerging merchant disputes or service issues
